maria (customer): Hey team — over the last 2 hours we've seen ~15 503s and a billing jump. Example request IDs: req_01H3K8X0A, req_01H3K9F2B. No change on our side. Can you advise minimal repro steps so we can gather logs?

sam (support): Sorry you're hitting this, maria. We'll help. Can you share a curl or SDK snippet that reproduces? Also attach any request IDs + timestamps.

maria (customer): attaching a sample curl we used earlier, it fails ~20% of attempts.

maria (customer): ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hello"}'
```

lee (oncall): thanks. can you re-run with an explicit x-request-id header so we can tie to logs? e.g. `-H \"x-request-id: <your-uuid>\"` and paste both the id and the exact timestamp (UTC) when it errored.

maria (customer): ok re-ran, got a 503 at 2026-11-02T16:03:47Z. request id I used: debug-req-20261102-1. Server returned: `{"error":"service_unavailable","message":"temporarily overloaded"}`

sam (support): good. alex from runtime is on the thread. alex, can you check those request ids against backend traces and also confirm whether any billing meter anomalies could be related?

alex (eng): looking now. A few notes so support knows what to collect quickly:
- full response headers (incl x-rw-request-id if present)
- a curl with `-v` or `--trace-ascii` to capture TLS/HTTP handshake info
- SDK debug logs (env var)

alex (eng): minimal repro snippets I ask customers to try: one-shot curl, python requests, node fetch, and a tiny go binary. If any fail intermittently, capture the request-id and timestamp.

sam (support): sending the short examples here — please run in order and paste output + request-id for any non-200.

sam (support): CURL (add X-Request-Id):
```
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \\n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "x-request-id: test-$(date +%s)" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"ping"}'
```

sam (support): Python (requests):
```
import requests
import uuid
req_id = f"py-{uuid.uuid4()}"
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')}","x-request-id": req_id},
    json={"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"ping"},
    timeout=15)
print(req_id, resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

sam (support): Node (fetch):
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const reqId = `node-${Date.now()}`;
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'x-request-id': reqId, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', input: 'ping' }),
}).then(r => r.text().then(b => console.log(reqId, r.status, b))).catch(e => console.error(reqId, 'ERR', e.message));
```

sam (support): Go (tiny):
```
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main(){
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(`{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"ping"}`)))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("x-request-id", "go-12345")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil{fmt.Println("ERR",err); return}
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("STATUS", resp.StatusCode)
}
```

alex (eng): two more quick troubleshooting commands for customers: 1) run `curl -Iv` to capture TLS handshake, 2) run the curl with `--connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15` to differentiate connect vs server processing issues.

sam (support): also please archive the SDK debug logs. For JS/Python SDKs set DEBUG=redwood* (or REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1) and re-run the failing request. Attach the log file.

maria (customer): ran the python snippet 10x, 2 failed with 503. Pasted outputs:
- py-7f2e9e1b-1 200 OK (first)
- py-7f2e9e1b-2 503 {"error":"service_unavailable","request_id":"req_01H3K9F2B"}

maria (customer): I uploaded verbose curl trace and python sdk log to the support portal (ticket 5632).

sam (support): perfect, thanks. alex — ticket 5632 has the uploaded traces. Can you correlate req_01H3K9F2B and debug-req-20261102-1?

alex (eng): grabbing traces now. quick note on billing: if many requests are retried by the client, that could explain the spike — we can check token counts + duplicate request IDs. If the client retried without honoring the x-request-id uniqueness, the system will count each attempt.

alex (eng): also asking infra to pull node-level queue length and worker crash logs around 2026-11-02T16:00-16:10Z.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: revision r-20261102-4573 to service/runtime at 2026-11-02T15:58:00Z :rocket:

lee (oncall): FYI, that deploy was a small tunable for batching. I'm checking if it could have transiently opened a backlog.

sam (support): next steps for customer: 1) if possible re-run with unique x-request-id per attempt (we recommend UUIDs), 2) keep verbose logs, 3) if you see retries from your SDK please disable automatic retries temporarily so we can count attempts.

maria (customer): will do. estimated time to collect another 50 runs ~20 minutes, I'll post results. Thanks for the quick help. :thumbsup:

alex (eng): thanks — we'll update ticket 5632 with correlation results once infra returns logs. If we confirm a short-term overload during that window we'll propose a mitigation (rate-limiter tweak + automatic fallback to smaller model).

sam (support): sound plan. leaving this thread open until correlation complete. If you hit any new request IDs, paste them here.

maria (customer): uploaded the extra runs: 50 runs -> 3 failures, IDs included in the portal.

lee (oncall): infra found a transient worker restart at 2026-11-02T16:02:43Z that aligns with a small spike in queue latency. Collecting full stack traces now.

alex (eng): thanks, that explains the intermittent 503s. For billing concerns we'll check whether retry patterns produced duplicate meter events — will follow up in the ticket.

sam (support): closing loop later in ticket but summarizing here for others: minimal repro steps we asked for = curl with x-request-id, python/node/go minimal calls, SDK debug logs with DEBUG env, verbose curl traces, and single-run non-retry attempts. That package helps trace and resolve both 503s and billing double-counts quickly.

maria (customer): great, appreciate the clear minimal steps.

sam (support): :white_check_mark: thanks everyone.
